_comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for every headline number on this platform. Frontend, RESULTS.md, and the demo script must read/copy from this file only — never hand-type a number. This kills landing/board/RESULTS drift permanently (Phase 0.3). Every value carries a `source` pointing at committed evidence. `open_items` records known conflicts to reconcile in the Phase 4.4 consistency sweep.
status: evidence-complete for core measurement claims: isolcpus run committed, bare-metal p99 MEASURED (7.7µs), Firecracker seccomp boundary ENFORCED + proven (verified_runs/aftab/firecracker_*), 4 protocol loops Sent==Acked CI-verified. Surface propagation (76x CO, measured 7.7µs, run-dependent bytes, design-target labels removed) is DONE. Pending: a committed isolated-host per-protocol latency run to promote WS/FIX/REST p99s from representative to measured; and the multi-node >=3-node distributed scale run (~30k target).

naming.note: The core hot-path wire is a custom binary SBE-style protocol (fixed 4B header + fixed structs); the BINARY board cites SBE v1. As of Phase 3.2-3.4 the platform ALSO benchmarks WebSocket, FIX 4.4, and REST as additional transports (bot -> adapter -> reference engine, Sent==Acked CI-verified in wsrest-build.yml). Binary remains the hot path; the other three exist to measure the framing tax (binary << WS << FIX << REST). Per-protocol ABSOLUTE latency is representative (shared CI runner) until a committed isolated-host latency run is logged to verified_runs/.

planted_bug.bug: LIFO matching instead of FIFO price-time priority
planted_bug.note: Buggy journal is the SAME length as the correct one (852 bytes) — a threshold checker passes it; the byte-exact diff catches it.

byte_exact_replay.claim: Live TCP server output journal == offline replay, byte-for-byte (diff exit 0)
byte_exact_replay.note: The byte COUNT is run-dependent — fill count varies with the order stream. Committed runs measured IDENTICAL at 25,743,624 (ARCH_LINUX_RUN), 25,759,344, and 25,797,720 (verified_runs/aftab/live_replay.txt, 200k/200k, 309,962 fills) bytes. What reproduces every time is the INVARIANT claim: live == offline, IDENTICAL, exit 0. Surfaces cite 25,743,624 as the representative figure; never present it as a fixed constant — lead with the identical-match claim, not the number.

run.host: Arch Linux 16-core, no isolcpus (shared dev host)

headline_gap.basis: p99 naive 173µs → CO-corrected 3.41ms, the fully-tabulated shared-host run
headline_gap.host_range: 19.7x (shared host) up to 76x (isolcpus) — host-dependent: the cleaner the host, the harder naive lies, because the baseline drops while the planted 5ms stall stays fixed
headline_gap.isolcpus_run: verified_runs/aftab/co_proof.txt (i7-13620H, isolcpus): naive p99 41,119ns → CO 3,135,487ns = 76.3x, 600k/600k acked, 49,566 phantom backfilled
headline_gap.note: 19.7x is the conservative tabulated headline (judge can verify line-by-line). The isolcpus run measured 76.3x — above the old '20-75x' band, so the range is now 19.7x-76x. Earlier prose cited ~35x (a ~98µs naive baseline, no committed table) — that is retired. Surfaces should say '19.7x tabulated, up to 76x on isolated hardware'.

spsc_offload.note: Lock-free SPSC ring; CI asserts dropped==0 on every push.

scale_32bot.note: Committed figure 1,279,594. Newer isolcpus run reports 1,279,829 — throughput-bound, varies per run; both show Sent==Acked, 0 lost/double-counted.

shared_host.note: un-isolated / shared host; scheduler jitter dominates the tail. This is the deliberately-hostile measurement environment.

baremetal_measured.host: Intel i7-13620H, isolcpus=0,1 nohz_full=0,1 rcu_nocbs=0,1, clean run (no planted stall)
baremetal_measured.note: MEASURED, not a target: p99 = 7.7µs on isolated cores (300k/300k acked, EAGAIN=0). Naive == CO (ratio 1.0) because a quiet isolated machine has no coordinated-omission gap to hide — the methodology's own honesty check. This RETIRES the 'design target — not yet measured' label: delete every such label from RESULTS.md, README, ARCHITECTURE, frontend, and publish 'measured p99 7.7µs on an isolated consumer desktop (i7-13620H), not server hardware'.

scale_thousands.note: Thousands-capable demonstrated on one box: 2989 concurrent connections, 3.6M orders. Under extreme oversubscription the bot THROTTLES (PoolExhausted, EAGAIN) rather than lose or double-count — Sent and Acked stay within 44 across 3.6M (in-flight-at-shutdown + 16 partial aborts), 0 collisions, 0 double-counts. Backpressure made visible, not hidden. Label it exactly as 'scale + accounting under backpressure', not latency. The clean 1000+-per-node run is the distributed Phase 2.3.
